"The interface uses one shared set of colours, spacing and corner radii. "This release brings the M9 frontend redesign into the main branch as a single version." - Supported by #244.

"and keep card titles from shrinking below their content width" - The #240 fix wraps the title and sets min-width: 0 so a long unbreakable title can shrink; the flex shrink fix (flex: 0 0 auto) came from #213 and concerned cards, not this fix.

"Citations in assistant answers: Assistant answers now show citations as badges placed where the answer uses them, and hovering or focusing a badge shows the source, heading and snippet." - This duplicates the inline citation badges item and is based on #233's AnswerCitationLayout, which #244 removed and replaced with #245; it is listed as a separate feature.

"Changing a ticket's status or assignee is done from a menu in the ticket header. The ticket stays open and keeps its scroll position and current tab" - The facts support this for #234 (menus/popovers), but the claim does not mention that these inline menus stay alongside other controls; this is minor. The live popover was not browser-tested.

"The release v1.9.0 brings the Frontend Redesign milestone into the main branch." - Supported by #244, but the output's opening says the release 'completes' the milestone and lists assistant reliability fixes (M10 scope from v1.8.0, #220-#223) as part of this release. Those were in v1.8.0 per #224.

"Grounding check always runs: When the assistant has retrieved knowledge-base passages, it now checks its answer against them before responding" - #218 forces the check only once after retrieval, not always, and belongs to v1.8.0 (M10).
"Agent names known to the assistant: The assistant now knows the names of the active agents when it answers" - #221 is M10 / v1.8.0 work, not part of v1.9.0 per #224.

"Render streamed assistant citations as inline badges placed after the cited passage title, with a focusable tooltip, and keep a numbered sources list as fallback for unanchored citations." - The facts say the inline badges from #233 were deferred and replaced by a sources list when #244 merged. Inline badges were later re-introduced over Markdown in #245. Listing #233 as a separate shipped feature mischaracterizes the release, because #233 was superseded and is a duplicate of #245.

"with a hover and focus tooltip showing title, source and snippet" - #245 says the tooltip shows the title, source › heading, and snippet. The output drops the heading, which is minor. The tooltip claim itself is supported, so this is a minor wording difference.

"You get a verified answer in every such case, not one that depends on whether the model chose to check." - The facts say the check is forced once after retrieval and the verdict is not surfaced to users; it does not guarantee every passage is grounded or that the user gets a verified answer.

"so the screen always reflects what the server holds." - The facts only say status renders optimistically and reconciles with the server, with a guard against superseded moves; 'always' overstates this.

"A failed knowledge-base search is now reported as an error, distinct from a search that found nothing or was unavailable" - The facts distinguish failed from unavailable, but do not say anything about a search that found nothing.

"Citations in the assistant's answers are linked to the passages they support, and a sources list appears under the answer for any citation not placed inline. Hovering a citation shows its source, heading and snippet, and answers without citations look as they did before." - This is a duplicate, older description from #233, whose AnswerCitationLayout was removed in the integration (#244) and replaced by the Markdown-based badges of #245; it also says an answer without citations renders unchanged, which describes the superseded implementation.

"Render streamed assistant citations as inline badges placed where the model cited a title, with a focusable tooltip, and fall back to a numbered sources list for citations not anchored inline, leaving answers without citations unchanged." - #244 says that #207's inline badges were dropped in the integration (Markdown leads, badges deferred to #243), so this is not a shipped feature of the release as a separate item; it is superseded by #245.

"Replace the assign and change-status dialogs on the ticket detail page with inline menu popovers that apply changes in place through the same command handlers, keeping scroll position and open tab, and remove the two dialog components." - The facts do not describe anything contradicting this; however the PR says live popover open/click was not driven in a browser, so the claim is supported only by design. (Minor.)

"Hovering or focusing a badge shows the source, heading and snippet, so you can check each claim without leaving the answer." - The facts say the tooltip shows title, source › heading, and snippet; the 'check each claim without leaving the answer' benefit is not stated. Also, the first bullet on inline citation badges duplicates the later citations bullet.

"The check runs on every grounded answer, so you no longer depend on the model choosing to run it." - The facts say the check is forced once after retrieval (force-once), not on every grounded answer; it guarantees at least one check after any retrieval, not each answer.

"The assistant now checks each knowledge-base-grounded answer for support in the retrieved sources before it finishes." - The facts say enforcement is force-once after passages appear, and the verdict is not surfaced to users; it is not a per-answer user-visible check.

"Answers that match the sources in meaning are no longer marked as ungrounded for using different wording." - The facts say the semantic path is not deterministic and falls back to lexical scoring without a Voyage key or on embedding failure, so this overstates the guarantee; the verdict is also not surfaced to users.

"Add inline citation badges with a hover and focus tooltip to assistant chat answers through `AnswerCitationLayout`, keeping a numbered sources list for unanchored citations." - The facts say #244 removed `AnswerCitationLayout` and its tests when Markdown rendering took the lead, deferring inline badges to #243. The output presents this as a shipped release feature without noting that it was removed.

"Citation badges in assistant chat: Assistant citations can now appear as inline badges in the answer text, with a tooltip showing source, heading and snippet on hover or keyboard focus." - This restates #233 (plain-text badges via AnswerCitationLayout), which #244 removed in favor of Markdown plus a sources list, replaced by #245. Listing it as a separate shipped feature duplicates the inline badges bullet and is misleading.

"The assistant page shows formatted answers with citations in a sources list below, and the grounding score no longer appears in the transcript." - The facts say inline badges were re-introduced by #245 in v1.9.0, so describing citations as only a sources list below contradicts the final state. Also, the grounding chip removal was a conflict resolution, not a user-facing 'no longer appears' change.
"so you can trust what the board shows." - This is an overstated benefit not stated in the facts; the facts only describe optimistic apply, rollback and a concurrency guard.

"Titles are now limited to two lines with an ellipsis, so cards in a lane keep a consistent height there; newer Chrome versions were not affected." - The facts say the bug did not reproduce on Chrome 149, a single tested version; 'newer Chrome versions were not affected' generalizes beyond what was verified.

"and board card titles are no longer cut off mid-letter." - The mid-glyph clipping fix (flex: 0 0 auto) is stated in #213, but the claim is a loose paraphrase of it; this part is supported, but it sits among broader unsupported styling claims.

"Render assistant citations as inline badges with a hover and keyboard-focus tooltip by splitting the answer with `AnswerCitationLayout`, keeping the numbered sources list for citations not anchored inline." - Per #244, `AnswerCitationLayout` and its tests were removed during integration (Markdown leads, inline badges deferred to #243), and #245 re-introduced badges differently via `AssistantMarkdown.Render`. This entry describes a superseded implementation as a shipped feature.

"You can rely on the button doing the same thing as the manual controls, so you no longer have to open them for the suggested step." - The facts say the action goes through the same handler as the manual path; they do not say users no longer need the manual controls. The generic controls stay always available.

"Citation badges in chat: Assistant answers can show numbered citation badges with a tooltip on hover or keyboard focus giving source, heading and snippet. Citations not anchored in the text stay in a numbered sources list" - This describes #233's plain-text badge feature (AnswerCitationLayout), which #244 removed in favour of Markdown-led sources lists. The entry duplicates the inline badge feature and describes a superseded implementation.

"Version 1.9.0 brings the full Frontend Redesign into one release. Assistant answers render as formatted text with citations in a sources list below" - Citations in a sources list below the answer was the interim state in #244. The final release, per #245, anchors inline badges in the Markdown answer as well as listing the sources, so this describes a superseded state.

"so times match the ticket detail view and due dates carry your offset." - The facts say the UTC offset stays in the format string so the model expresses due dates with the user's offset; they do not guarantee that due dates carry your offset.

"Render assistant citations as inline `[n]` badges with a hover and focus tooltip, computed by the new `AnswerCitationLayout`, with a numbered sources list as fallback for unanchored citations." - #244 says `AnswerCitationLayout` and its tests were removed when Markdown rendering took precedence over inline badges, and the badges were deferred to #243. So the shipped release does not contain this feature as described.

"Assistant answers can now show numbered citation badges tied to the claims they support, with a tooltip on hover or keyboard focus showing source, heading and snippet." - This bullet duplicates the earlier citation badges entry, built from #233 (the first-version feature). #244 states that implementation was dropped in favor of the sources list and inline badges were deferred, then re-added by #245. Presenting #233's CSS-only layout as a separate shipped feature is not supported.

"You can now count on the screen not holding a status the server never accepted, including after two quick changes on one ticket." - The facts only say the move-sequence guard prevents the board from holding a rejected status. The detail view only restores the previous ticket on rejection. The guarantee is overstated for the detail view.

"You can rely on at least one check having run after any retrieval, for both the chat assistant and the autonomous worker." - The enforcement guarantees only that a check is forced once after passages appear. The facts say it does not guarantee every retrieved passage was grounded before the final answer.

"Long ticket titles on board cards could grow the card without limit in some older Chrome versions." - The facts describe the bug as occurring on Chrome and say it is not reproducible on Chrome 149. Naming 'older Chrome versions' is an inference, not a stated version scope.

"Assistant sources list: Citations in assistant answers are now listed as a numbered Sources list below the answer. An answer without citations shows no empty Sources block." - The Sources list below the answer was the interim #244 integration state, and #245 re-adds inline badges while keeping the sources list for unanchored citations. The 'no empty Sources block' claim comes from #233. Presenting it as a separate new feature is misleading.

"You can count on that check having run for every answer drawn from the knowledge base" - #218 says the check is forced only once, on the first turn after passages appear. It guarantees at least one check after any retrieval, not that every passage or answer was grounded. The claim overstates this.

"a citation the answer does not quote by title still appears in that list, as long as the assistant quotes the passage title word for word, which it is instructed to do." - The facts say a citation whose title does not appear stays in the sources list only. Anchoring (not the list entry) depends on the model quoting the title verbatim. The sentence garbles this condition.

"Board card titles no longer get cut off mid-letter." - The design-token PR (#213) says the card titles clipped mid-glyph and that it fixed this with flex: 0 0 auto. Listing it under 'Consistent look across pages' attributes it to the wrong feature, though the fix itself is supported.

"The assistant now always checks such an answer at least once before it starts replying, so the check no longer depends on the assistant choosing to run it." - Facts say the check is forced once after retrieval via tool_choice, but not that it 'always' holds for every case; however mostly supported. The overstated 'always' is minor, yet the facts also say it guarantees only one check after any retrieval, not every passage.

"and header and row cells stay aligned in both light and dark themes." - The fact only says the Category column got a 140px width and alignment stayed intact; verification was at 1600px, and the facts do not mention checking both themes beyond the acceptance criterion text.

"On older Chrome versions, a long ticket title on the board could stretch its card without limit." - Supported in substance, but the claim that titles are now cut to two lines was not observable as fixed on older Chrome; the facts say the bug did not reproduce on Chrome 149 and the fix is inert there.

"Citations in assistant answers can now appear as numbered badges next to the text they support, with a preview of the source, heading and snippet on hover or keyboard focus." - This duplicates the inline badge entry, but is based on #233's AnswerCitationLayout, which #244 removed in favor of the Markdown-anchored approach in #245, so it is not a separate delivered feature.

"Instant status changes: ... so what you see always matches what was saved." - Facts describe optimistic updates with rollback and reconciliation, but the optimistic drag was not driven in a browser and 'always matches' overstates the guarantee.

"The v1.9.0 release brings together the M9 frontend redesign, with changes to ticket workflows, assistant responses, and the interface." - The M9 integration and release are supported, as are interface and assistant changes, but the broad summary’s claim of changes to ticket workflows is not established as a release-wide description by a single fact.

"**Inline citation badges:** Cited passage titles in assistant Markdown answers can show numbered badges, with a preview on hover or keyboard focus. The badges match the numbered source entries, and citations without a matching title remain in the source list." - The badges have tooltips with title, source, heading, and snippet, but the description does not say they provide a preview. It says unmatched citations remain in the sources list; it does not qualify this as citations “without a matching title” in the same way—the documented limitation is that anchoring relies on the model quoting the passage title verbatim. The output repeats this feature again later.

"**Suggested ticket actions:** The first actionable suggested step appears as a button or agent picker on a ticket, while other steps remain in an overflow menu." - The primary control is based on the first suggested step, and actionable steps are ordered first. However, not all other steps necessarily remain in an overflow menu: unmapped steps render as non-clickable text, and advisory steps can be disabled.

"**Inline citation badges:** Citations can appear as numbered badges beside matching titles in assistant answers, with source details available on hover or keyboard focus. Unmatched citations remain in the numbered sources list." - The tooltip includes source, heading, and snippet, but “source details” omits the stated heading and snippet only by being broad; the unsupported meaning is “beside matching titles,” which does not capture the documented placement after the cited passage title and can imply a general title match. More importantly, badges are described as reintroduced on sanitized Markdown and rely on verbatim title quoting; this duplicated claim is not independently supported as phrased.

"**v1.9.0 release:** This release brings the M9 frontend redesign together in a single release, including updated ticket workflows and assistant features." - The M9 integration is supported, but the statement characterizes the release as including updated ticket workflows as a whole. No single fact makes that release-wide claim; the relevant PR describes integrating M9 and adding release notes.

"**Board card titles:** Long board card titles now stop at two lines with an ellipsis. Cards in a lane remain bounded in height." - The fix is described as applying to titles longer than two lines, and bounded card height was verified for the test case. The output states this without that condition and implies the behavior is universal, while the fact also notes the browser used could not reproduce the targeted older-Chrome bug.

"**Assistant confirmation policy:** The assistant no longer claims a change succeeded unless a tool reports success, and it carries out changes the user has already requested without asking again. It still asks for confirmation when the request involves a genuine decision, such as an ambiguous ticket match or uncertain intent." - Write honesty requires that the tool call be made and its result report success in the conversation. The output omits the requirement that success be reported in the conversation. The policy also allows confirmation for missing required information and hard-to-reverse actions with real doubt about intent, which the examples do not fully convey.

"**Summary timestamps:** Timestamps in ticket summaries are shown in the configured user timezone. Summary times match the ticket detail view, so you can rely on the same local time in both." - The facts say timestamps are converted using the configured timezone, matching the ticket detail view. “You can rely on the same local time in both” overstates this: it asserts a general guarantee about displayed summary times, whereas the fact specifies the timestamp conversion supplied to the model/prompt.

"**Grounding by meaning:** Grounding checks now assess whether answer sentences are supported by retrieved passages, including when they paraphrase or translate them." - The semantic evaluator supports paraphrases and translations, but the fact explicitly says the check still counts some non-claims such as greetings and follow-up questions as substantive sentences, and does not close the whole-answer-scoping problem. The output presents the capability without this limitation.

"previews available on hover or keyboard focus" - PR #245 supports a hover/focus tooltip. PR #233 describes the earlier inline implementation, but the integrated v1.9.0 release notes in #244 say Markdown leads and inline badges were deferred to #243; #245 is the implementation reintroduced over sanitized Markdown. The output's duplicated entry is otherwise broadly supported, but this wording is supported by #245, not evidence of two separate delivered implementations.

"with changes to ticket views, assistant chat, and interface styling" - The v1.9.0 integration PR describes the M9 frontend redesign and release notes, but does not characterize the release as containing the assistant grounding and error-handling changes listed elsewhere in this changelog. As a claim about the release as a whole, it rephrases no single fact.

"The assistant could ask for confirmation again after you had already requested a change" - PR #223 says the specific needless double-confirmation field scenario was not reproducible in five live turns before this change; the missing policy was what remained. The output presents the behavior as an established prior defect rather than a policy gap addressed by the change.

"The assistant could ... claim a change without a successful tool result" - PR #223 describes write honesty as a prompt rule to prevent unsupported claims, but its live reproduction says the original field behavior was not reproducible. The output states that the assistant did make such claims as a confirmed prior behavior.

"Correct paraphrases and translations could be marked as ungrounded because the check relied on word overlap." - PR #219 supports this, but the output omits the specific limitation that the grounding check still has an open whole-answer-scoping problem: non-claim sentences with content words may be counted. The heading and summary imply the grounding defect is resolved without that qualification.

"The assistant now reports a change only after its tool call succeeds, and carries out changes users have already requested without asking again." - The change adds system-prompt instructions requiring write honesty and discouraging needless confirmation; it does not mechanically guarantee this behavior. The facts explicitly describe model behavior as not pinnable by the scripted evaluation suite and verification as a limited live pass. The output presents the instructed behavior as an unconditional behavioral guarantee.

"Add system-prompt rules that prevent the assistant from claiming a write succeeded without a successful tool result" - The PR adds a prompt policy instructing the assistant not to claim a successful write without a successful tool result; it does not establish that the rules prevent such behavior. The facts explicitly distinguish the prose policy from guarantees about model behavior and describe verification through a live pass.

"You can rely on it to use names from the roster, or list the valid agents when the requested name is not present." - The roster is injected into the chat system prompt, which instructs the model to use exact roster names and list valid agents for an unknown name. The facts establish prompt instructions, not a guarantee that the model will always follow them.

"The assistant no longer claims a change was made unless a tool reports success, and it does not ask for confirmation when you have already requested a change. You can rely on it to ask only when a decision or missing information warrants confirmation." - The change adds write-honesty and confirmation rules to the system prompt, verified in a limited live pass; it does not guarantee future model behavior. The facts also explicitly permit confirmation for ambiguous ticket matches, missing required information, hard-to-reverse actions with genuine doubt about intent, and uncertain route_ticket suggestions, even when a change has been requested.

"The assistant no longer asks for confirmation after you have already requested a change, including after correcting an earlier mistake." - The change adds a system-prompt policy against needless confirmation, not an unconditional prohibition or guarantee of model behavior. Confirmation remains legitimate for ambiguous ticket matches, missing required information, hard-to-reverse actions with real doubt about intent, and uncertain route_ticket suggestions.
